parallel.requirements: The prompt required every file under /workspace/requirements to be read and implemented; the harness listed 193 remaining requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent used native AgentSwarm in three rounds, assigning 45 grouped implementation owners, then 128 single-slug owners, then 95 private-worktree owners.
parallel.implementation: Only three visible requirement patches were produced: atomic durable transaction support, on_commit callable validation, and has_perm obj-argument test fixes.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered patch timeline stabilized at exactly three requirement_patches files; most delegated work never reached delivered patch artifacts.
parallel.verification: One completed child reported focused transaction tests and the official harness later marked the task resolved; no full 193-requirement agent verification is visible.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Large active swarms were cancelled with 44, 128, and 95 aborted children, leaving 190 of 193 required patch artifacts visibly absent despite the official pass.

serial.requirements: The serial run received the same prompt and counted 193 requirement files with zero requirement patches at the start.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run had one main actor, no AgentSwarm or subagents, and no decomposition beyond two Bash inspections.
serial.implementation: The serial run made no visible implementation changes and produced no requirement_patches files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: There was no integration or delivery activity because no patch artifacts were created in the serial trajectory.
serial.verification: The agent did not run focused implementation tests before failing; the official harness nevertheless recorded all final test results as passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The main serial turn ended on provider.rate_limit after reading one requirement, with the patch timeline still empty.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel prompt required reading and implementing all 193 requirement files, and the parent explicitly noted all 193 before spawning children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial prompt had the same 193-requirement obligation and the main agent counted 193 requirement files before doing anything else.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both saw the full task size, but parallel attempted to distribute the full set while serial only surveyed it and did not implement any requirement before failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the task into AgentSwarm batches: first 45 grouped assignments, then 128 single-slug assignments, then 95 two-slug worktree assignments.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation and performed only local Bash inspection commands in a single main-agent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created many implementation owners but terminated them; serial had one owner and no child ownership graph.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs contained slug lists, requirement-reading instructions, test guidance, commit protocol, and later private-worktree boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained all context in one main session and inspected the repository and one requirement directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The record does not show a missing child brief or interface contract as the deciding issue; the problem occurred after context transfer when active child work was cancelled.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced concrete patches for atomic durable transactions, on_commit callable validation, and has_perm obj argument tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced no requirement patch files and no code changes before the provider error ended its turn.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implemented three visible requirements, while serial implemented none despite both being marked resolved officially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel stopped active child batches: round 1 completed one and aborted 44, round 2 aborted 128, and round 3 aborted 95.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; its main turn ended failed after repeated provider rate-limit retries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost active delegated implementation work through cancellation, whereas serial never created child work to join or cancel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final observed parallel patch timeline contained only three requirement diffs even after later rounds; round 3 also shifted work into private worktrees requiring later promotion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial never created patch files, so there was no integration or shared-state assembly to inspect.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left a partial delivered artifact set after cancelled delegated work; serial left an empty delivered artifact set.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: One completed child reported focused transaction tests, and the official harness later marked the task resolved.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial shows no agent-run tests before the provider-rate-limit failure, yet the official harness later marked the task resolved.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The official pass is not aligned with the visible agent work in either trajectory; parallel had limited child verification for three patches, serial had no implementation verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed three rounds with AgentSwarm usage and ended process_ok false while evaluator status still recorded a pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used only two Bash calls, ended process_ok false from a provider rate limit, and still received an official pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent large budget on cancelled child batches; serial spent little budget and stopped from provider rate limiting, so their official identical outcomes mask very different closure states.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations mark both modes as solution_passed true, so there is no official outcome discordance. Process evidence is nevertheless sharply different: parallel partially implemented three requirements through cancelled swarms, while serial produced no patches and ended on a provider rate-limit error. The equal official pass is therefore treated as an evaluator/status effect, not as proof of equivalent task-solving work.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used three AgentSwarm rounds and delivered exactly three requirement patches before cancellation stopped active child work.
serial_contributors: Serial used no delegation, made only two Bash inspections, produced no patch files, and ended with provider.rate_limit.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented three concrete Django changes; serial did not implement any visible code or patch artifact.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluations report resolved despite trajectory evidence showing only partial or no visible implementation artifacts.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is adverse process evidence only

candidates.reason: Rejected: implementation owners were explicitly assigned through AgentSwarm child items; the observed failure was cancellation of those active owners, not absence of an owner.
Rejected: no set of independently completed component implementations is shown to need unresolved integration; the material issue is aborted child execution before most components existed.
Rejected: the required patch-file delivery workflow was specified, and no complete unassembled candidate set is shown; cancellation preempted assembly.
Rejected: the parent controlled the multi-round workflow and evaluator lifecycle; the concrete defect is active child termination, not an unowned end-to-end transition.
Rejected: productive implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parallel run launched implementation swarms directly.
Rejected: the parallel investigation was not a separate all-investigation phase deferring implementation; children were instructed to implement and commit changes.
Rejected: there is no separate indispensable path starved by auxiliary work; the same observed chain is explicit cancellation of active implementation children.
Rejected: broad fan-out and deadline pressure are visible, but the more specific direct boundary is explicit cancellation before child results finalized.
Rejected: some children had multi-slug assignments, but no single oversized child is proven as the cause; later one- or two-slug swarms were also cancelled.

Rejected: child prompts included the requirement slug(s), instruction to read the YAML, implementation scope, tests, and commit protocol; no known parent requirement is shown omitted from a child brief.
Rejected: the evidence does not show independently completed components with incompatible interfaces or missing interoperation contracts.
Rejected: no known finding or checkpoint is shown present before transfer and absent after transfer; most child work was stopped before handoff.
Rejected: no returned handoff containing needed information is shown to be too large or too poorly structured for the parent to consume.
Rejected: no receiver is shown acting on a superseded handoff or outdated workspace state.
Rejected: no incompatible completed reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
Rejected: the parent did not make a non-evaluator whole-task completion decision; final response files are empty and the official status alone cannot create this label.
Rejected: later rounds changed strategy and scope and reflected knowledge that three patches already existed; repeated unfinished work is better explained by the cancellation chain.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Retained: the parallel parent launched active AgentSwarm batches and then explicitly cancelled them before needed work or results finalized, leaving only three delivered requirement patches.
candidates.realized_consequence: Active implementation swarms were stopped before needed work finalized, leaving only three delivered requirement patches for a 193-requirement task.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover would describe the downstream lack of recovery after aborted children, but the directly evidenced boundary is cancellation itself and earlier cancelled scopes were partly reassigned in later rounds.

candidates.reason: Rejected: no complete promotable candidate or compatible component set existed before closure; the unfinished pieces were interrupted by cancellation.
Rejected: no child result is shown being merged only after integrated verification with no post-merge check.
Rejected: the one completed child result produced visible patch files, while the rest of the delegated implementations were aborted rather than completed and ignored.
Rejected: no verifier child with a concrete finding is shown trapped below the parent before closure.

Rejected: cancelled children and lack of final recovery are downstream of the same explicit cancellation chain; earlier rounds also attempted reassignment, so this would duplicate Early Child Termination.
Rejected: the completed child result was reflected in requirement patch files; no available completed result is shown ignored at a decision point.
Rejected: waiting and timeout pressure are visible, but the decisive event is explicit cancellation of active children, not failure to inspect available progress.
Rejected: no competing cross-file implementations or designs requiring reconciliation are proven from the raw trajectory.
Rejected: no two live agents are shown editing the same source file and requiring reconciliation of concurrent edits.
Rejected: no agent is shown replacing or wholesale rewriting another agent owned non-entry source file.
Rejected: no required executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact is shown overwritten by another actor.
Rejected: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion is shown replacing another actor final-tree work.
Rejected: early shared-workspace work did not produce a concrete unstable-state or provenance problem distinct from cancelled children; round 3 used private worktrees.
Rejected: no generated artifact, cache, fixture, or temporary file from one actor is shown contaminating another actor execution or verification.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the explicit child-cancellation chain met the retention gate.
